features.name: Academic Preparation
features.description: The level of formal academic training or credential the letter presents as relevant preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is stated, or the educational background is unclear.
States a bachelor's degree or equivalent practical preparation in a relevant technical field.
States a master's degree in a relevant technical field.
States a doctoral degree in a relevant technical field.

features.name: Agentic Systems Design
features.description: Experience designing agent-based systems with bounded autonomy, orchestration, and supporting infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic Fluency
features.description: Concrete evidence of applied data-structures-and-algorithms skill in real engineering work.

levels.descriptor: No evidence of algorithmic strength is given.
The letter claims strength in algorithms or data structures without a concrete example.
The letter gives one clear example of algorithmic or data-structure improvement.
The letter gives multiple or especially strong examples tied to meaningful system simplification, performance, or correctness gains.

features.name: Applied AI Production Experience
features.description: Whether the applicant has actually built and operated AI or LLM-backed systems in production, with attention to reliability.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Developer Enablement and Collaboration
features.description: A user-centered, collaborative view of security tooling as helping developers and internal partners succeed with less friction.

levels.descriptor: No explicit developer-enablement framing appears.
The letter shows a general desire to help teams, but not specifically through security workflows or defaults.
The letter clearly states that security should assist developers rather than merely police them.
The letter shows a strong secure-by-default philosophy with empathy for busy engineers and attention to embedding good behavior into everyday workflows.

features.name: Distinctive Voice
features.description: How memorable, individualized, and non-templated the letter's framing or prose feels.

levels.descriptor: Highly formulaic prose with little individual voice.
Competent but generic prose with only limited individuality.
Includes a memorable framing device, belief, or personal thesis.
Sustains a distinctive, authentic voice throughout while still serving the application's purpose.

features.name: Engineering Rigor and Maintainability
features.description: Emphasis on reliability, maintainability, testing, correctness, and long-term operability in engineering work.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Evidence Specificity
features.description: How much the letter substantiates claims with concrete technical examples, mechanisms, or specifics rather than abstractions.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists qualities or interests with little supporting evidence.
Includes a few examples but limited detail on ownership or effect.
Gives concrete examples of work with enough detail to make the claims credible.
Repeatedly ties claims to specific actions and clear outcomes or impact.

features.name: Go Depth
features.description: How central and substantial Go appears in the applicant's real production engineering work.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Impact Articulation
features.description: How clearly the letter states the outcomes or practical effects of the applicant's work.

levels.descriptor: Lists tasks with no visible outcomes.
Hints at benefit but remains mostly activity-based.
States clear outcomes such as reduced manual work, faster systems, or fewer bugs.
Shows strong leverage language, tying work to capacity, attention saved, or meaningful organizational effect.

features.name: Language Breadth
features.description: The breadth of programming-language exposure beyond the role's core language requirements.

levels.descriptor: No additional languages are mentioned.
Mentions 1 to 2 additional languages.
Mentions 3 to 5 additional languages.
Mentions more than 5 additional languages.

features.name: Narrative Cohesion
features.description: Whether the letter forms a coherent overall story or career arc rather than a disconnected checklist.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like disconnected bullets, fragments, or stacked claims.
The letter has some structure, but transitions or the overall arc are uneven.
The letter coherently links background, technical experience, and interest in the role.
The letter presents an especially well-shaped narrative that makes the applicant's trajectory and fit feel natural.

features.name: Offensive Security Practice
features.description: Ongoing hands-on adversarial or offensive-security practice outside ordinary development work.

levels.descriptor: No adversarial practice outside normal work is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional participation or casual practice without depth signals.
The letter shows regular or serious engagement in adversarial exercises.
The letter shows unusually strong external practice, such as near-top finishes or another high-commitment signal.

features.name: Open-source Stewardship
features.description: Responsibility for contributing to, maintaining, or stewarding public code used beyond the applicant's employer.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance described.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
Shows active contribution or maintenance with review or release responsibility.
Maintains a used project or framework with sustained community, release, review, or user-support responsibilities.

features.name: Ownership Level
features.description: The level of autonomy, seniority, or direct responsibility the letter claims over the work described.

levels.descriptor: Mostly aspirational language or support-role contribution.
Shows some hands-on contribution but limited ownership.
Shows clear ownership of tools, systems, or reviews.
Shows repeated architecture, design, or lead responsibility with independent judgment.

features.name: Personal Project Ambition
features.description: The technical ambition, scope, and seriousness of self-directed engineering projects outside formal work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform Leverage Orientation
features.description: Motivation toward foundational infrastructure or platform work whose benefits compound across many teams.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production Delivery Scope
features.description: The breadth of hands-on responsibility for shipping, maintaining, operating, or owning real production systems.

levels.descriptor: Production scope is vague or very limited, with at most one clearly owned service.
The letter shows clear responsibility across about 2 production services.
The letter shows repeated production delivery across about 4 services.
The letter shows broad production breadth across 6 or more services or similarly wide operational scope.

features.name: Python Depth
features.description: How concretely the letter shows Python as a substantial production language for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is not mentioned.
Python is mentioned only briefly or as a light scripting tool.
The letter shows regular Python use for tooling, automation, analysis, or services.
The letter shows deep, production-grade Python ownership, such as typed or tested services, broad internal tooling, or heavy operational reliance.

features.name: Relevant Software Experience
features.description: The overall depth or duration of directly relevant professional software-engineering experience the applicant claims.

levels.descriptor: Below the role minimum or unclear on relevant experience length.
Roughly meets the minimum, around 2 to 3 years of relevant experience.
Shows solid mid-level experience, around 4 to 5 years.
Shows strong experience depth, around 6 or more years.

features.name: Role-specific Fit
features.description: How specifically the letter explains and maps the applicant's motivation and background to this exact role and mission.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security Assessment Experience
features.description: Hands-on experience evaluating systems for security issues through review, threat modeling, analysis, or remediation follow-through.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security Automation Insight
features.description: Understanding of the role as a high-leverage problem of scaling security expertise through automation and systems design.

levels.descriptor: Shows little role-specific framing beyond wanting security impact.
Shows general interest in secure defaults or automation, but not a sharp view of the problem.
Clearly frames security tooling as a way to scale review, response, or manual workload.
Frames the problem sharply in terms of scarce expert attention, organization-wide signal handling, variant analysis, or systems-level leverage.

features.name: Security Credentials
features.description: The presence and rigor of formal external security certifications or credentials.

levels.descriptor: No formal security credential is mentioned.
A baseline credential is mentioned, such as Security+, indicating foundational security study.
A stronger hands-on credential is mentioned, such as OSCP, indicating practical offensive testing ability.

features.name: Security Engineering Worldview
features.description: A thoughtful security-oriented philosophy, identity, or value system beyond listing tools or experience.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: Vulnerability Triage Automation
features.description: Direct experience building automation for vulnerability intake, classification, routing, deduplication, or related workflows.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling automation is described.
Shows general automation interest, but not with a concrete vulnerability triage example.
Describes a clear example of automating vulnerability intake or routing.
Describes a strong triage automation example with several functions such as classification, deduplication, prioritization, routing, or measurable manual-load reduction.

features.name: Writing Polish
features.description: The surface quality of the writing, including proofreading, spelling, grammar, and copy accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.
